html:
SMTO-EML-0013 — SMTO needs your approval before sending this email

GUID: ecb11d82-dae6-5b18-b91e-b07d3c82fd8a
Slug: email-confirmation-required
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • SMTO only sends an email after someone approves that exact message, and this send arrived without an approval. Nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in the conversation to send the email again. When the Approval needed card appears, check the sender, recipients, subject and attachments it shows. The card shows exactly what will go out, so you approve the right message.
  2. Select Approve once to send just this email, or Deny / stop task if anything looks wrong. Approve once covers only this exact email and nothing else.
  3. If you expected this email to send without asking, ask the person who manages SMTO to check Settings › Security › Policy / Permissions. Email goes out without a prompt only when a permission setting allows it.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the mail server accepted the message after your approval.

If it still fails

  • If the approval card never appears, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't give blanket permission just to get one email out; approve this one instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An email.send call reached the Email skill without its exact confirmation and without full_access approval mode, so it was refused before any preparation or network activity.

What this means

  • A send reaches the skill without its exact confirmation and without applicable full-access approval policy. Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.

Why this can happen

  • A send reaches the skill without its exact confirmation and without applicable full-access approval policy.

How to diagnose it

  • Review the current fixed sender, recipients, subject and attachment count attached to the exact operation.

How to fix it

  • Re-run the send through the normal approval flow so the confirmation carries the saved sender profile revision, recipients, subject and attachment count, or use approval_mode full_access (Settings › Security › Policy / Permissions or the composer's Permissions control) only if unattended sending is intended.
  • Review the saved sender profile, recipients, subject and attachment count, then approve this exact send.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended send is authorized through its supported policy before dispatch.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
